problem: Existing navigation-instruction generators (Speaker-Follower and EnvDrop speakers) encode full 360° panoramas with LSTMs and are poorly grounded. They lean on language priors, so they hallucinate objects and confuse left and right. As a result, humans reach only about 42% SR following their instructions on R2R val-unseen, against 75% for human-written instructions.
motivation: Good generated instructions could drive conversational wayfinding aids and supply near-unlimited synthetic data for VLN agents. Instruction generation differs from captioning: annotators look at under 30% of the environment and mention only a fraction of what they see. Feeding full panoramas therefore invites spurious correlations. RxR's pose traces and word timestamps give weak spatiotemporal grounding that can be used to find which visual regions people actually talk about.
key_idea: The paper bootstraps 971k silver landmark groundings from RxR pose traces using CTC-finetuned MURAL image-text alignment. It trains a detector to pick a few landmarks along a route. A multimodal mT5 then verbalizes only those landmarks, interleaved with templated orientation and action phrases ("less is more").
insight: Restricting the generator's visual input to a few salient landmarks sharply improves human followability. On R2R val-unseen, human SR is 57.8 for the full-pano SpkFol* trained on RxR, 64.9 for outbound views only, and 70.8 with detected landmarks, close to the 74.9 human ceiling. The authors attribute the gain to landmarks rather than architecture, because the transformer with MURAL features and full panos gets similar BLEU/CIDEr to SpkFol* (5.6/9.6 vs 5.7/8.4). The HAMT-follower SR does jump from 29.6 to 50.7 in that same comparison, so architecture is not irrelevant. A second lesson is that n-gram metrics mislead: switching from silver to predicted landmarks cuts CIDEr from 31.7 to 7.5 (prior-work level), while human SR stays nearly unchanged (61.5 vs 63.3). Smaller findings: a timestamp prior improves grounding precision (49.6→56.5, timestamp alone 23.4); the Rewrite auxiliary task gives +7.1 val-unseen CIDEr; CC3M/12M pretraining helps BLEU/CIDEr but not SPICE.
method: Landmark phrase extraction: a 3-layer distilled mBERT Universal-Dependencies parser finds entity heads and absorbs their non-clausal dependents into NP spans. Per-language manual stoplists (e.g. 'the room', 'step') filter the spans. The result is 971k phrases from 102k RxR instructions (84,237 unique; 9.55 per instruction).

CTC landmark grounding: logits are A_ij = MURAL_text(t_i)·MURAL_img(r_j) − λ(T(t_i) − T(r_j))², with λ=1. A trainable layer on the frozen MURAL-large encoders is trained with CTC loss (phrase order as target, BLANK for frames without a landmark). Greedy CTC decoding then keeps the highest-probability frame for each phrase.

Landmark refinement: many alternative perspective crops (heading, pitch, FOV) overlapping the selected frame are sampled. The crop with the highest MURAL score for the phrase becomes the silver landmark image.

Landmark detector: a single-class CenterNet with a COCO-pretrained Hourglass-104 backbone runs on 512×256 equirectangular panos. Each pano is rotated so the outbound direction is centered, colored pixel blocks mark inbound and outbound directions, and 90° circular padding is added. Training is 20k iterations at batch 128. At inference the top-3 detections per pano are pooled and the top-T kept (T = number of panos).

Multimodal mT5-base generator: 640-d MURAL landmark embeddings plus a per-pano 'outbound landmark' view are interleaved in an English template. The template uses 12 relative-orientation phrases and 12 action phrases (30° arcs each). A prompt, 'Translate placeholder template to English/Hindi/Telugu:', selects the output language. Landmarks within 5° on the same pano are de-duplicated.
Rewrite auxiliary task: during training, silver landmark image features are replaced by their text phrases, which teaches the model to map input landmarks to their surface realization.

Pretraining and finetuning: pretraining is multimodal caption translation with a pivot image on CC3M+CC12M (captions MT'd to Hindi/Telugu, only the first half of the caption given; 1.45M steps, Adafactor). Finetuning uses RxR train in all 3 languages with silver landmarks for 200k iterations, and decoding is argmax.

setting.backbone: Multimodal mT5-base encoder-decoder (fine-tuned) conditioned on frozen MURAL-large image embeddings (Google, not publicly released); CenterNet Hourglass-104 landmark detector (COCO-pretrained, fine-tuned). Task is instruction generation (a speaker), not a navigation agent.
setting.model_size: mT5-base (parameter count not stated in paper; mT5-base is ~580M)
setting.training_data: RxR train (en/hi/te) with 971k bootstrapped silver landmark groundings. Landmark phrases were extracted from RxR Train+Val-Seen+Val-Unseen; the detector and generator are trained on train-split silver data. Pretraining uses CC3M+CC12M image-caption pairs machine-translated to Hindi/Telugu. MURAL is pretrained on 1.8B image-text pairs and 6B translation pairs; the detector backbone on COCO 2017.
setting.observation: Sequence of 360° panoramas (equirectangular) along a given route, with inbound/outbound headings
setting.action_space: N/A for the model (outputs a text instruction). Human followers evaluate on the discrete Matterport3D nav-graph in PanGEA.
setting.simulator: Matterport3D (PanGEA annotation tool for human wayfinding; HAMT agent in Matterport3D simulator for automatic eval)
setting.privileged: The ground-truth route (panos and headings) is the generator's input by task definition. The main 'Predicted' variant uses no other privileged info. The 'Silver' variant uses landmarks derived from human pose traces/instructions of the evaluated paths (quasi-upper bound, not deployable).

numbers_note:
This is an instruction-generation (speaker) paper, not a navigation agent. SR/SPL/NE/nDTW are measured with human wayfinders (PanGEA) or a pretrained HAMT agent following the generated instructions, so the numbers are NOT comparable to VLN agent results on R2R/RxR. Custom 'other:' benchmark names are used for that reason.

Reference points:
- Human-written instructions: R2R val-unseen SR 74.9 / SPL 66.4; RxR val-unseen SR 78.4 / nDTW 69.2; HAMT on human instructions SR 56.5.
- Prior speakers on R2R (human eval): Speaker-Follower 42.0, EnvDrop 41.7, SpkFol* (RxR-trained) 57.8.

Per-language RxR human wayfinding SR (Supp. table, N=1,517 each):
- Predicted: en 61.3, hi 59.4, te 63.9
- Silver: en 65.0, hi 60.7, te 64.2
- Outbound: en 52.8, hi 50.8, te 56.3
- Human: en 77.5, hi 77.1, te 80.9

Inconsistencies:
- The abstract's '61-64% SRs on three languages' does not exactly match the Predicted per-language values (Hindi is 59.4).
- The intro's '58% for our model trained on full 360° panos' matches the Table 1 SpkFol* row (57.8), not a Marky-mT5 full-pano row.
- Table 3 prints no SPL; SPL for HAMT comes from the supplementary table.
results: On R2R val-unseen paths, human wayfinders reach 70.8% SR / 59.8 SPL following Marky-mT5 instructions with predicted landmarks. This compares with 74.9% for human instructions, 42.0% (Speaker-Follower), 41.7% (EnvDrop) and 57.8% for Speaker-Follower re-trained on RxR. On the longer RxR val-unseen paths across en/hi/te, humans obtain 61.5% SR vs 78.4% for human instructions; silver landmarks raise this to 63.3% and outbound-only views give 53.3%. A HAMT agent follows Marky-mT5 instructions nearly as well as human ones (55.7 vs 56.5 SR; nDTW 63.3 vs 62.9), yet BLEU/CIDEr with predicted landmarks fall to prior-work levels.
limitations: The generator is blind to broader environment context when generating, so it fails at pragmatic reasoning (e.g. 'Leave the room' when there are multiple exits). A clear gap to human instructions remains on long RxR paths (61.5 vs 78.4 SR). In error analysis, only 16% of instructions are error-free and weak landmark descriptions make up 62.9% of errors.

Silver-landmark bootstrapping assumes landmarks are mentioned in the order they are seen, and grounding precision is modest (56.5 on 100 manually checked instructions). The pipeline also depends on Google-internal MURAL-large features and pose-trace data that only RxR provides.

Evaluation relies on costly human wayfinding (20k evaluations, 70 India-based annotators). Standard automatic text metrics (BLEU/CIDEr/SPICE) were shown to be inconsistent with human judgments across landmark sources.
compares_to: SpkFol* (Speaker-Follower re-implemented and trained on RxR)
